covers.quote: Use the term ‘Defence’ when you mean both the Department of Defence and the Australian Defence Force (ADF). ‘Defence’ is used to represent the organisation as a whole.

examples.note: Formal reference to the organisation as a whole uses capital D.

parts.quote: Defence engages with industry to deliver procurement outcomes that support departmental and ADF capability.
The institute’s paper examines the implications for our defence strategy over the next decade.

rules.quote: ‘Defence’ has an initial capital when it is part of a formal name or title. Use lower case for generic references.
rules.specification: Capitalise 'Defence' when referring to the organisation as a whole (Department of Defence + ADF) or in formal titles; use lowercase 'defence' for generic references.
rules.violation_condition: the word 'defence' capitalized in generic references, or lowercased when referring formally to the organisation or in a formal title
when: Use 'Defence' with an initial capital when it represents the organisation as a whole or is part of a formal name or title.
Use lower case for generic references.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 consolidate the naming definition and capitalisation rules into one rule governing Defence capitalisation.

covers.quote: When referring to the services, follow the order of precedence established by the Defence Act 1903:

examples.note: Services listed in precedence order: Navy, Army, Air Force.

parts.quote: Defence Reserves are an essential part of the Navy, Army and Air Force

rules.quote: Follow the order of precedence for the 3 arms of the ADF
rules.specification: When referring to the three arms of the ADF collectively, order them: Navy, Army, Air Force.
rules.violation_condition: mentioning the three services together out of the order: Royal Australian Navy (Navy), Australian Army (Army), Royal Australian Air Force (Air Force)
when: When listing or referring to the services together.
rules.why: The heading directly states the actionable ordering requirement (G-4).

parts.quote: Defence Reserves are an essential part of the Navy, Army and Air Force

rules.quote: Always use initial capitals when writing the short names of the services:
rules.specification: The short names 'Navy', 'Army', and 'Air Force' must have initial capital letters.
rules.violation_condition: writing the short names of the services ('Navy', 'Army', 'Air Force') in lower case
rules.why: Direct prescriptive rule on capitalisation of service short names.

covers.quote: Address members of the ADF by rank, name and post-nominals
Do this:

examples.note: Rank, given names, family name, post-nominals, service.

parts.quote: Rear Admiral Robert W Plath AM RAN

examples.note: Rank, given name, family name, post-nominals.

parts.quote: Lieutenant General Susan Coyle AM CSC DSM

rules.quote:
Use the following order to address members of the ADF:

* rank
* given name or initials
* family name
* post-nominals
* service (for commissioned officers in the Navy only).
rules.violation_condition: addressing or mentioning an ADF member in full with components out of the order rank, given name/initials, family name, post-nominals, service
when: the first time you write their name in body text
in address blocks in correspondence
when introducing an ADF member as speaker
in official records of proceedings
in lists in organisational publications such as annual reports
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 consolidate the heading and its trigger circumstances into one rule.

examples.note: Subsequent mention uses rank and family name only.

parts.quote: Chief Petty Officer Rosendale now has a role advising the Navy on First Nations cultural affairs.

rules.quote: If you mention the name again in body text, use rank and family name.
rules.violation_condition: subsequent mentions of an ADF member in body text using given names or failing to use rank and family name
when: When mentioning an ADF member again after the first mention in body text.
rules.why: Specific rule for subsequent mentions in body text.

covers.quote: Only one rank has a hyphen
There is one exception from the Air Force: Air Vice-Marshal. It is always hyphenated.

parts.quote: Acting Sub Lieutenant DW Midson RAN
Air Vice-Marshal Catherine Roberts AM CSC

rules.quote: Write military ranks of more than one word as separate words. Do not hyphenate the rank.
rules.specification: Military ranks of more than one word are not hyphenated, except Air Vice-Marshal which is always hyphenated.
rules.violation_condition: hyphenating a multi-word military rank other than 'Air Vice-Marshal'
when: Except for Air Vice-Marshal, which is always hyphenated.
rules.why: G-2 consolidates the general rule and its single exception.

examples.note: No commas between or before post-nominals.

parts.quote: Commander Algirdus Diciunas MBE CSM RAN

rules.quote: Don’t use commas before or between post-nominals.
rules.violation_condition: a comma placed immediately before or between post-nominal letters
rules.why: Specific punctuation prohibition on post-nominals.

covers.quote: Use ‘RAN’ to indicate Navy service for commissioned officers
Don’t use an acronym to show service for officers in the Army or Air Force.

parts.quote: Captain Stephen Beckmann AO CSC RAN [Navy]

examples.note: Army officer does not include service acronym.

parts.quote: Captain Catherine Wilsen AO [Army]

rules.quote: Use ‘RAN’ (Royal Australian Navy) for all commissioned officers of the Navy. Place ‘RAN’ after the family name and any post-nominals.
rules.violation_condition: omitting 'RAN' after the family name and post-nominals for a commissioned Navy officer, or using service acronyms for Army or Air Force officers
when: Do not use an acronym to show service for officers in the Army or Air Force.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 fold the negative restriction for Army/Air Force into the rule governing RAN service designation.

covers.quote: Write the rank before the title of ADF members who are knighted

parts.quote: General Sir John Monash GCMG KBE VD

rules.quote: When someone has a military rank and another title such as ‘Sir’, ‘Dame’ or ‘the Honourable’, place the military rank first.
rules.violation_condition: placing a civil title or honorific ('Sir', 'Dame', 'the Honourable') before a military rank
rules.why: G-4: the body sentence is more general and accurate than the heading.

covers.quote: Address chaplains and maritime spiritual wellbeing officers by title

parts.quote: Principal Chaplain Darren Jaensch [Army]

rules.quote: Address chaplains with their chaplaincy title, not a military rank.
rules.violation_condition: addressing an ADF chaplain with a military rank instead of their chaplaincy title
rules.why: G-2 / G-4 addresses the rule for chaplains.

parts.quote: Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer Tammy Dunne [Navy]

rules.quote: MSWOs have been part of the Navy since 2020. Address them with their MSWO title, not a military rank.
rules.violation_condition: addressing a Maritime Spiritual Wellbeing Officer with a military rank instead of their MSWO title
rules.why: Specific rule for addressing maritime spiritual wellbeing officers.

covers.quote: Address retired officers of the ADF by rank

parts.quote: General the Honourable Sir Peter Cosgrove AK CVO MC (Retd)

rules.quote: Commissioned officers who retire can continue to use their military rank. When writing their name, use their rank and include ‘(Retd)’ after any post-nominals.
rules.violation_condition: omitting '(Retd)' after post-nominals when addressing or writing the name of a retired commissioned officer retaining military rank
when: Applies when writing the name of retired commissioned officers who retain military rank.
rules.why: G-2/G-4 combines heading and instruction.

covers.quote: Avoid using the shortened forms of ranks

examples.note: Full rank spelled out with initial capital.

parts.quote: Lieutenant T Smith [Outside Defence]
LT T Smith [Defence only]

rules.quote: Don’t follow this convention in other types of content. Write the full rank with an initial capital letter.
rules.specification: Outside internal Defence content, do not abbreviate military ranks (such as LT); spell out the rank with an initial capital letter (Lieutenant).
rules.violation_condition: using an abbreviated rank (e.g. 'LT') in non-internal Defence content
when: In non-Defence content.
rules.why: G-4 marks the operative instruction under the heading.

rules.violation_condition: post-nominals included in a correspondence salutation
rules.why: Clear negative instruction for salutations.

rules.quote: Never add a comma after salutations.
rules.violation_condition: a comma placed after a salutation
rules.why: Clear punctuation rule for salutations.
